title: Check Point Security Management Servers Hacked in AI-Assisted Campaign
content_md: A threat actor has been using AI-enabled offensive tools in a broad campaign targeting Check Point Security Management servers, threat intelligence firm GreyNoise reports. As part of the campaign, which the security firm started tracking in early October and is likely still ongoing, a threat actor tracked as GreyNoise Threat 13 (GT13) has been conducting scanning, exploitation, and control activities from 99 IP addresses, many associated with disposable network infrastructure. According to GreyNoise, GT13 targeted at least 22 organizations from the energy, engineering, financial services, government, manufacturing, mining, and transportation sectors across the US, the UK, Australia, Austria, China, France, Germany, Hong Kong, the Netherlands, South Korea, and other geographies. GreyNoise believes the threat actor has been using agentic harnesses and systems to weaponize vulnerabilities, find vulnerable assets, and automatically exploit them. The automated operations were complemented by hands-on-keyboard activity. “We witnessed the GT13 actor use 99 IP addresses, all of which were either egresses through ExpressVPN or compromised victim Check Point devices, including activity over 1400+ network sessions, 800+ command line artifacts, and 1200+ files downloaded, uploaded, or created,” GreyNoise says .
